speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin our assessment, how long has this lesion been present and has it changed in size or appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Necrotizing Fasciitis.

I have reviewed your history of Crohn's, diabetes, and recent corticosteroid use, which significantly impairs your immune response. The rapid progression from a bite to a large ulcerative lesion over one month is highly concerning for a severe, life-threatening soft tissue infection. I need to immediately check your vital signs and request a tissue culture and MRI to confirm the extent of the infection and guide treatment. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Blood_Culture, Lactate. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Leg.
